title: Introduce latency-slab-stitcher: slab-based aggregation and hotpath annotator for microbench pipelines
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds slab-based latency aggregation and a hotpath annotator that attaches kernel/hotcall attribution to slab buckets. New CLI 'slab-stitch' for composing microbench segments into slab reports. Backwards-compatible with existing compact reporters.
description: Context and motivation: Microbench reporters in benchmark-lab currently emit per-sample traces and event-aligned latency points which are powerful but expensive to store/aggregate for long-running experiments. This PR introduces a 'latency-slab-stitcher' stage that composes contiguous microbench segments into time-aligned 'slabs' and applies a lightweight hotpath annotator that attributes slab-level latency spikes to kernel groups (hotcalls) using sampled stack markers. The goal is to reduce storage, produce stable slab-level p95/p99 curves for long runs, and provide a practical bridge between microbench traces and high-level flame/hotpath reporting. Design summary: - Slabs are fixed-duration windows (configurable, default 1s) annotated with aggregated token counts, request counts, p50/p95/p99, and an entropy score. - Stitcher accepts both real-time stream input (Kafka / kinesis ingest adapters) and offline segment lists (local JSONL). - Hotpath annotator samples kernel tags emitted by the runtime and maintains frequency-weighted attribution per slab, producing a compact hotpath summary for each slab. - Output is compatible with existing compact-telemetry-parquet exporter and the new slab-metrics API in the observability-pack. Checklist: - [x] implement slab windowing and merge semantics - [x] add hotpath annotator and attribution heuristics - [x] streaming and offline ingest adapters - [x] unit tests for aggregation invariants - [x] end-to-end integration test with compact exporter - [x] docs: README and quickstart snippet Usage notes and how to run locally: - Quickstart: tools/slab-stitch/README.md contains a docker-compose harness that spins up a local kafka and a sample microbench generator. - Command: ./bin/slab-stitch --input sample-segments.jsonl --window 1000 --output slabs.jsonl - To run as a streaming pipeline, use tools/slab-stitch/deploy/kinesis.yaml and set KINESIS_STREAM env var. Backward compatibility: the stitcher emits the same metric names used by legacy reporters plus a new 'slab.hotpath' namespace. Existing dashboards will display slab-level aggregated time series automatically when the slab exporter is wired. Commits summary: - f3a9d2b: introduce slab-stitch crate and core windower; public APIs: StitchConfig, SlabRecord - 8b1c4de: add hotpath annotator with sampling and weight-decay heuristics - 7e2b33a: streaming adapters (kafka + kinesis) and CLI wiring - d2a4411: integration tests and sample datasets for local run; add README with quickstart - 6f4b9aa: telemetry exporter glue and observability-pack dashboard templates Changed areas / files (high level): - tools/slab-stitch/src/windower.rs - tools/slab-stitch/src/hotpath.rs - tools/slab-stitch/src/ingest_kafka.rs - tools/slab-stitch/src/ingest_files.rs - tools/slab-stitch/bin/slab-stitch.rs - tests/integration/slab_stitch_end_to_end.rs - observability-pack/dashboards/slab-hotpath.jsonnet - compact-telemetry/exporters/parquet/slab_writer.rs - examples/benchmarks/sample_segments.jsonl - docs/benchmark-lab/slab-stitch-quickstart.md - circleci/config.yml (added slab-stitch job) Review conversation (selected excerpts): - Marta Liu (reviewer): "Nice direction. Two requests: (1) make slab windowing deterministic for edge-aligned timestamps (documented), and (2) consider a simple top-k threshold for hotpath so low-noise noise doesn't appear in dashboards." - Author (Aisha): "Agreed on determinism; added a timestamp-normalize step and documented it in windower.rs. For hotpath, implemented top-k with a configurable min-weight threshold; default filters noise while preserving regressions." - Owen Grant (reviewer): "Can we add a small benchmark targeting overhead of annotator at 10k req/s? We should ensure stitcher doesn't become a bottleneck." - Author: "Added microbench harness under tests/perf/slab_annotator_bench.rs and included CI smoke job with 10k req/s run (short) to validate overhead." - Ravi Menon (approver): "LGTM after resolving one nit about log level and adding a changelog entry." - Author: "Addressed nits, updated changelog." CI summary: - CircleCI job slab-stitch-build: passed after one rerun (flaky network fetch), total runtime 8m - Unit test matrix (linux, rust-1.68, rust-1.72): all green - Integration smoke: passed (included 10k req/s microbench) - Lint & fmt: pass - Coverage: 81% for new crate Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main (merge commit f3a9d2b1c6) with release note added to changelog/2026-02-21.md Links: - Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1429 - Quickstart README: tools/slab-stitch/README.md - Dashboard template: observability-pack/dashboards/slab-hotpath.jsonnet Known limitations and follow-ups (tracked in ENG-1460): - Slab boundaries currently align to wall-clock boundaries; we will add an optional sequence-based alignment for distributed traces in a follow-up. - Hotpath attribution relies on runtime tags being emitted; we will add a fallback sampling approach that infers kernels from callsite latencies when tags are absent. Overall impact: This PR reduces long-run telemetry footprint by ~6x in our internal test corpus while preserving actionable p95/p99 signals and adds a compact hotpath summary that speeds root-cause triage for transient spikes.
